answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing jobs funded from a shared escrow, with payment released after independent counterparties confirm delivery. A newcomer cannot gain much voting weight by minting identities: it must first lock scarce funds, do useful work, and risk losing its bond when reviews reveal fraud. This makes a sybil swarm costly to sustain, while gradual reputation growth acts like a glacier against a sudden tide of fake accounts; timber orders, for example, count only after verified delivery.
